text:
Droit de la famille — 151173

2015 QCCS 2309

JB 3083

SUPERIOR COURT

CANADA

PROVINCE OF QUEBEC

DISTRICT OF

MONTREAL

No:

500-12-320367-133

DATE:

MAY 26, 2015

______________________________________________________________________

IN THE PRESENCE OF:

THE HONOURABLE

SYLVIANE BORENSTEIN J.S.C.

______________________________________________________________________

N. A.,

Plaintiff,

v.

S. S.,

Defendant.

______________________________________________________________________

J U D G M E N T

______________________________________________________________________

[
1
]

Plaintiff asks for a divorce, the parties have
not lived together for more than a year, thus it will be granted.

[
2
]

It is in the best interest of the children that
the mother continues to have custody and that the father’s access be the same.

-      Every second weekend from Saturday 9:00 a.m.
to Sunday 6:00 p.m.;

-      Three days in the first week of the Christmas
holidays if father is not working;

-      One week during the summer holidays not to
interfere with camp and if the father is not working.

[
3
]

It will be from June 20
th
to June 26
th

2015 and, if the children do not have school, it will be March 3
rd

to 10
th
for 2016 which correspond to the father’s vacation.

[
4
]

The father will not be allowed to travel with
the children to any country which is not signatory of the Hague Convention.

[
5
]

The father will have Easter weekend provided it
does not coincide with Passover.

[
6
]

The mother will have the children for the Rosh
Hashanah, Yom Kippur and Passover holidays which they have always spent with
the mother’s family as although the father converted to Judaism when he got
married, no member of his family did or follow the Jewish holidays.

[
7
]

The relationship between the children and their
father is sometimes problematic.  The father has not yet accepted the break-up
and the mother’s new relationship.

He has exhibited his anger in front of the children who sometimes are scared.

[
8
]

Although, on December 9, 2013, he undertook in
front of Justice Turcotte not to harass or denigrate the mother in front of the
children, he has not respected his undertaking.

[
9
]

He has therefore made it difficult and expensive
for Plaintiff to get travel authorizations or to get the father to respect the
various judgments obtained.

[
10
]

He multiplied groundless proceedings and has not
provided the documents requested and ordered by the Court.

[
11
]

On the second day of the hearing, he sent an
email that he was at the emergency at the hospital.  Verifications showed he
had been discharged at 8:00 a.m.  Calls on his cellular and home phones were
unanswered.  He finally called and was told to present himself at Court, he
answered he could not as he did not have his papers.  He was told to go and get
his papers and come to Court as the hearing would take place.  He arrived
wearing his work uniform showing therefore that he had no intention to present
himself at Court and was at work.

[
12
]

This was an example of his attitude and
disrespect toward the Court and the many judgments given since the institution
of the proceedings during which he ended up representing himself after two
attorneys ceased representing him.

[
13
]

Although he signed a consent which was
homologated by Justice Courville whereby the parties would hire a joint expert
to determine the value of the family residence and share its costs, he hired
another expert later and did not pay his share of the cost of the joint
expertise.

[
14
]

Even though he agreed that the parties would go
directly to the merits as evidenced by the minutes of the hearing of August 22,
2014, he served a motion for provisional measures shortly after.

[
15
]

His examination of September 12, 2014 reveals
his aggressive and cavalier attitude, his refusal to answer and a significant
disregard for truth.

[
16
]

The Court, therefore, has to rely on the
documents produced by Plaintiff.

[
17
]

The Schedule I signed by the mother on March 4,
2015 and supported by the documents determines the child support to be
$1,432.79 a month including the special expenses.

[
18
]

There will be no spousal support.

[
19
]

The family patrimony consists of the family
residence, the moveable effects garnishing it, the father’s Honda Accord, the
mother’s RRSP, the father’s employment pension plan and the parties Quebec
pension plan.

[
20
]

The mother lives with the children in the family
residence and wants to acquire the father’s share in it.  The father is in
agreement.  The dispute centers on the value of the equity.

[
21
]

The joint expert determined the fair market
value at $315,000.00 which the Court accepts.

[
22
]

The expertise produced later by the father is of
no value; the expert had not even visited the house and was relying on pictures
taken in 2005.

[
23
]

The line of credit/mortgage is $222,000.00.

[
24
]

The net equity is $93,000.00.

[
25
]

However the proof establishes that the father
withdrew $62,000.00 from the line of credit which he has not been able to
justify.

[
26
]

The mother withdrew $7,000.00 which will also
have to be deducted.

[
27
]

Thus $93,000.00 + $62,000.00 + $7,000.00 =
$162,000.00 ÷ 2 = $81,000.00.

[
28
]

The father is therefore entitled to $81,000.00 -
$62,000.00 = $19,000.00.

[
29
]

The mother is entitled to $81,000.00 - $7,000.00
= $74,000.00.

[
30
]

However, from the father’s $19,000.00 must be
deducted what he owes pursuant to the judgments and what was paid by the mother
on his behalf:

-      Arrears from judgment of December 9, 2013

October 16, 2014 – March 16, 2015

$900.00 x
6
$5,400.00

-      Judgment of November 7,
2014                                                        $5,000.00

-      Interest payments made by the mother on the
capital

withdrawn by the father from the line of credit (Index I)

September 2013 – March 2015

$275.00 x
19
$5,225.00

-      Life insurance premium payments from the line
of credit (Index 2)

September 2013 – March 2015

$53.10 x
19
$1,008.90

TOTAL:                    $16,633.90

[
31
]

Thus the mother owes the father for his share of
the family residence: $19,000.00 - $16,633.90 = $2,366.10.

[
32
]

The mother will be granted sole ownership of the
moveable effects garnishing the family residence where she lives with the
children.

[
33
]

The father lives in his deceased mother’s house
which is fully furnished and which he inherited with his brother.

[
34
]

The father will remain owner of his Honda
Accord.

[
35
]

The mother owes the father $9,000.00 from her
RRSP.

[
36
]

As she is already getting $5,000.00 from Justice
Arcand’s judgment,

the Court will grant the mother a provision for costs of only $10,000.00 in
view of the multiplication of proceedings she had to initiate or contest
because of the unreasonable conduct of the father.

[
37
]

So the mother will keep the $9,000.00 as part
payment of the provision for costs.

[
38
]

Thus the mother will be sole owner of her RRSP.

[
39
]

The father will be sole owner of his employment
pension plan.

[
40
]

There will be equal partition of the parties’
benefits under the Quebec pension plan, accrued from March 21
st
,
2004 to November 22
nd
, 2013.

[
41
]

Because the father, despite the judgment on his
consent for joint expertise,

had his own expert produce another expertise and testifying, it was necessary
for the joint expert to analyze the other report and testify at the hearing.

[
42
]

The father should pay for his fees of $465.00 plus
taxes, for a total of $534.75, which will be deducted from the $2,366.10 of
equity in the house owed to the father.

[
43
]

Will also be deducted the balance of $1,000.00
on the provision for costs,

leaving $2,366.10 - $534.75 - $1,000.00 = $831.35 owed to the father for his
share of the family residence.

[
44
]

FOR THESE REASONS, THE COURT:

[
45
]

PRONOUNCES the divorce between the parties who
were married in Town A on the 21
st
day of March 2004 and will take
effect on the 31
st
day from the date of this judgment;

[
46
]

GRANTS the mother custody of Jaeden and Leah;

[
47
]

GRANTS the father access:

-      Every second weekend from Saturday 9:00 a.m.
to Sunday 6:00 p.m.;

-      Easter weekend when it does not coincide with
the first two days of Passover;

-      Three days in the first week of the Christmas
holidays provided the father is not working;

-      One week during the summer holidays not to
interfere with the children’s attendance at camp and if the father is not
working;

-      For 2015, the holidays will be from June 20
th

to June 26
th
provided the children have no school, as it coincides
with the father’s vacation period;

-      For 2016, the father’s vacation period is
March 3
rd
to 10
th
;

-      The father can have the children during that
time if they have no school.

[
48
]

ORDERS the father not to travel with the
children to any country which is not signatory of the Hague Convention;

[
49
]

ORDERS that the children be with their mother
for the Rosh Hashanah,

Yom Kippur and Passover holidays;

[
50
]

ORDERS the father to pay child support of
$1,432.79 monthly in accordance with Schedule I;

[
51
]

AWARDS unto Plaintiff sole ownership of the
family residence;

[
52
]

ORDERS Defendant to sign the deed of transfer to
confer sole ownership of the family residence unto Plaintiff within 15 days
following the present judgment upon payment by Plaintiff to Defendant of the
sum of $831.35;

[
53
]

IN DEFAULT whereof, ORDERS that the present
judgment shall avail in lieu of Defendant’s signature for said purpose;

[
54
]

AWARDS to Plaintiff the sole ownership of the
moveable effects garnishing the family residence;

[
55
]

AWARDS Defendant sole ownership of his Honda
Accord;

[
56
]

GRANTS Plaintiff a provision for costs of
$10,000.00 which has been compensated as described in the judgment;

[
57
]

DECLARES Plaintiff sole owner of the RRSP in her
name;

[
58
]

DECLARES Defendant sole owner of the employment
pension plan in his name;

[
59
]

ORDERS equal partition of the benefits accrued
pursuant to the
Act Respecting the Quebec Pension Plan
for the period of
March 21
st
, 2004 to November 22
nd
, 2013;

[
60
]

DECLARES the dissolution of the matrimonial
regime;

[
61
]

ORDERS provisional execution notwithstanding any
appeal;

[
62
]

THE WHOLE, without costs.

__________________________________

SYLVIANE BORENSTEIN J.S.C.

Me Robert Pancer

Phillips, Friedman,
Kotler

Attorneys for Plaintiff

S. S.

Representing himself

Dates of hearing:

March 5 and 6, 2015
